title: Warm halogen, cool LED: colour temperature
standards: MA MP-B Standard 5 (lighting, sets and props)

steps.text: Halogen lights like the room's Fresnels are warm (about 3200 K). Daylight LEDs are cool (about 5600 K). The camera's white balance decides which one looks white.
The halogen Fresnel as the key, with the camera set to Tungsten white balance to match it.

steps.question: Switch the camera's white balance to Daylight. What colour will the face turn?
steps.explain: Halogen light is much warmer than daylight. With the camera expecting daylight, the halogen looks orange.

steps.question: Back to Tungsten white balance, and add a daylight-balanced CB60 (5600 K) as a fill on the other side. What colour will the fill side look?
steps.explain: Mixing warm and cool lights gives two colours on one face. Here the camera matches the warm key, so the cooler fill looks blue.

steps.text: Fix it: make both sides of the face the same colour. You can change the fill's colour temperature, or swap it for a different light.
steps.hint: Pick the fill light, open Colour, and slide Warm ↔ cool down to 3200 K to match the halogen key.
